name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits; satellite warning
summary: Intelligence reports say Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite from December; Kremlin dismisses them
state: German broadcasters and Süddeutsche Zeitung reported on 23 Nov that Western intelligence, including Germany's BND and Bundeswehr, believes Russia could put a satellite carrying a nuclear explosive device, called Sputnik-S, into orbit as early as December; Russia's embassy said its space work is peaceful and Kremlin spokesman Peskov dismissed the reports (Meduza). No US–Russia treaty limits apply since New START lapsed. No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use in an active conflict was found to 25 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: There is no change to UK public guidance. Official information on emergencies is published by the UK government's Prepare service; follow it rather than speculation.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired) and reported nuclear-armed satellite plans; no test or alert change

sources.title: Meduza — Western intelligence services say Russia could put satellite with nuclear warhead into orbit in coming months

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
